oncall-bot: INCIDENT INC-2026 triggered: embeddings-queue-depth > 500 and consumer-lag > 120s. Paging primary. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-queue :rotating_light:
oncall-bot: Pager notes: top impacted service `embeddings-prod`, metric spike started ~1869999600. Escalation threshold hit.
oncall-bot: Bridge: #incident-bridge-1869999999 created.

sam: I'm primary until 06:00 UTC. Quick handoff summary: issue started ~21:40 UTC, customers seeing long tail latency and occasional 503s for batch embedding requests. No data loss.

sam: Active alerts:
- embeddings-queue-depth > 500 (main queue)
- embeddings-consumer-lag > 120s
- retries-onwrite > 1000/min
- pod OOM spikes on worker-3 (g4-3)

sam: Actions taken so far:
- Scaled consumer deployment `embeddings-consumers` from 3 -> 6 (temporary).
- Applied soft rate limit on upstream batch router: 50 rps -> 20 rps for non-prem tier.
- Rotated worker-3 (restarted pod, moved weight to worker-1/2).
- Enabled fallback model for low-priority traffic to `embeddings-small-quant` (reduced mem/cpu).
- Kicked a manual manual requeue to drain slowest messages.

sam: Commands I ran (for context):
```bash
# scale up consumers
kubectl -n prod scale deployment embeddings-consumers --replicas=6
# patch router rate limit
kubectl -n prod patch configmap batch-router --patch '{"data":{"rate_limit":"20"}}'
```

sam: Current status: queue depth down from ~720 -> ~260 in the last 18m. Errors still elevated but tail latency improving. Ongoing risk: worker OOMs may reappear because of large pinned batches; we should consider lowering max_batch_size.

lee: noted. Do we have telemetry on which customers are hitting the largest batches?

sam: yes — dashboard split by org: `dashboard/embeddings/queue-by-org`. Top orgs: acme-inc, searchlabs, smallpilot. Acme accounts for ~48% of large batches.

maria: I'm taking secondary until 02:00 UTC, then I'll switch to primary at 02:00. If things look stable I'll continue, otherwise escalate to infra oncall.

sam: coverage note: Maria has a calendar conflict 23:30-00:15 UTC (short meeting). Aj agreed to stand by during that window as secondary.

aj: I'll be reachable for pages during 23:30-00:15. If I get paged I'll start by checking mobile alerts then run the `emb-quick-check` script.

sam: Runbook pointers (important):
- Quick triage: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-queue#triage
- Fallback policy: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-queue#fallbacks
- How to reduce OOM: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-queue#oom-mitigation

sam: Immediate next steps for whoever is primary:
1) Watch queue depth and consumer-lag (alerts already muted for noisy thresholds until we stabilize).
2) If queue depth stops falling for 10m, reduce `max_batch_size` from 1024 -> 512 on consumer config and roll small canary.
3) If OOMs continue on any worker, cordon node and move traffic away: `kubectl cordon <node>` + drain then scale.
4) Keep rate limit in place until tail < 300 for 20m.

devops-bot: Scheduled autoscaler cooldown adjusted: minReplicas=3 maxReplicas=12.

sam: Customer impact summary for handoff note to CS:
- Symptom: longer embedding response times (median +200ms, p99 up to +8s).
- Error class: intermittent 503s on batched endpoints for non-prem tiers (estimated <0.6% of requests in last 30m).
- Scope: ~3% of total embedding requests affected; high impact for heavy batch customers (acme-inc).
- Mitigation: rate limiting + fallback reduced visible errors; most customers now see degraded perf not complete failures.

cs-bot: Notifying CS: message queued to `#customer-alerts` with suggested copy. Cc @cs-sre.

lee: Anything the on-call needs from infra/SRE now?

sam: Possible infra asks in next 30-60m if OOMs continue:
- quick node replacement (g4-3) if restart doesn't hold
- temporary quota bump for worker memory limits to avoid frequent OOMs while we lower batch size

maria: I'll start the `max_batch_size` canary at 02:10 UTC (after I become primary) unless you want me to do it earlier.

sam: Fine with that. I'm going offline in 20m but will leave detailed logs in the bridge. If pages fire and Maria unreachable, Aj is backup.

lee: small nit — make sure to annotate the deploy that changes `max_batch_size` with `incident=INC-2026` so rollback is easy.

sam: will do. Also added a short healthcheck we can toggle: `curl -s https://internal.health/emb-consumers | jq .queue_depth`.

maria: quick ask — can someone confirm whether the dedicated ACME traffic is on a separate route? If not, we might temporarily bump them to dedicated path as emergency workaround.

sam: ACME uses shared route but flagged as premium. There's an existing bypass we can toggle (requires infra approval).

lee: tagging infra oncall: @infra-oncall please standby for possible bypass toggle and node replacement.

sam: final note: logging aggregated at `s3://prod-logs/incidents/INC-2026/` — I uploaded `consumer-stacktrace-21-49.log`.

aj: ack. I'll be up if pages come through.

maria: I'll take over as primary at 02:00 UTC and post a new summary then. Good handoff, thanks. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Thread auto-closed for inactivity (no messages for 60m). If the incident re-escalates a new thread will be created.
